To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the path-integral of the nonlinear sigma-model can be written as the path integral of the SU(3) Haar measure with an SU(3) invariant action.

the path integral over the non-linear SU(2) sigma-model, in terms of the flat SU(2) connection, can be defined by a functional integral over the SU(2)-group, and that the ancestor amplitudes are the only relevant quantities in this functional integral.
the path-integral measure over the non-linear SU(2) sigma model, which is the fundamental object of our research, can be defined in terms of a path integral over a non-linearly realized group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the derivation of the full Green functions for the pion fields of a nonlinear sigma model in a background gauge field.
the problem of deriving the perturbative expansion of the full Green functions in terms of the ancestor amplitudes.
the problem of the construction of a non-perturbative regularization of the path-integrals of the non-linearly realised group.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the path-integral formulation of the SU(3) nonlinear sigma model is not only possible but is in fact the most natural and convenient way to formulate this model.
the perturbation theory of the nonlinear sigma models can be defined in terms of the path-integrals over the non-linear groups.
the perturbative path-integral over SU(2) is defined by the Haar measure of SU(2) and the nonlinear sigma-model constraint.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have solved the problem of the path-integration over the non-linear SU(2) sigma model.
we are able to solve the problem of the path-integration over the non-linear group SU(2) in terms of a hierarchy of ancestor amplitud...
we are able to derive the full Green functions in the nonlinear sigma model, order by order, in the loop expansion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the path-integral is a well-defined functional integral in the sense of Schwinger.
the ancestor amplitudes of the nonlinear sigma-model can be obtained from a perturbative expansion of the Haar measure.

this path-integral is well defined, even if the nonlinear sigma model action is singular, as long as we restrict the integration to the space of paths that satisfy the nonlinear sigma model condition.
